title: Blend gravel to a fines window

blocks.text: A county roads department buys road-base gravel from several pits. Each pit has a price per ton, a *fines* content (the share of very small particles, in % of weight) and the tons it can supply. The specification says the delivered gravel's average fines content must lie between `low` and `high` percent: too few fines and the base will not compact, too many and it drains badly.

With $`J`$ the pits, $`p_j`$ the price per ton, $`q_j`$ the fines content (%), $`u_j`$ the tons pit $`j`$ has, $`T`$ the tons needed and $`[\ell, h]`$ the window, the average rule $`\ell \le \sum_j q_j t_j / \sum_j t_j \le h`$ is multiplied out by the total tons:

\begin{aligned}
\min \;& \sum_{j \in J} p_j\, t_j \\
\text{s.t. }& \sum_{j \in J} t_j = T && && \text{(tons)} \\
& \sum_{j \in J} (q_j - h)\, t_j \le 0 && && \text{(fines\_max)} \\
& \sum_{j \in J} (q_j - \ell)\, t_j \ge 0 && && \text{(fines\_min)} \\
& 0 \le t_j \le u_j && \forall j \in J
\end{aligned}

$`t_j`$ is continuous: the tons bought from pit $`j`$. Write `mix(pits, tons, low, high)` in `blend.py`. It solves this model with GLOP and returns `(status, cost, tons_by_pit)`: the name of the termination reason; when it is `OPTIMAL`, the cost and a dict from pit name to tons (not rounded, every pit included); otherwise `None, None`.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pit:
    name: str
    price: float      # $ per ton
    fines: float      # fines content, % of weight
    tons: float       # tons the pit can supply


def mix(pits: list[Pit], tons: float, low: float, high: float):
    """Cheapest blend of `tons` tons whose average fines content lies in [low, high]."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="gravel blend")
    t = {p.name: model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=p.tons, name=f"t_{p.name}") for p in pits}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(t.values()) == tons, name="tons")
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum((p.fines - high) * t[p.name] for p in pits) <= 0, name="fines_max")
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum((p.fines - low) * t[p.name] for p in pits) >= 0, name="fines_min")
    model.minimize(sum(p.price * t[p.name] for p in pits))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.GLOP)
    status = result.termination.reason.name
    if result.termination.reason != mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL:
        return status, None, None
    return status, result.objective_value(), {name: result.variable_values(v) for name, v in t.items()}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pits = [Pit("A", 12, 4, 500), Pit("B", 9, 9, 600), Pit("C", 7, 14, 400)]
    print(mix(pits, 1000, 6, 10))

cases.says: the cheapest blend delivers the tonnage with its average fines inside the window
the average must also stay at or above the lower limit, even when low-fines gravel is cheapest
a pit supplies at most the tons it has
a window no blend can reach gives INFEASIBLE with no cost and no blend

origin.section: A Blend Rule Bounds an Average, and the Average Is Linear Once Multiplied by the Total

concepts: an average-quality rule is multiplied by the total and written as one row per limit
